extracted.intended_audience: authors querying literary agents / aspiring authors seeking representation
extracted.subtask_description: An individual literary agent's manuscript wishlist and submission guidelines describing which genres, subgenres, themes, age categories, and submission materials he prefers or rejects, plus personal taste signals to help authors target queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction: genres wanted
rubrics_metrics.description: In fiction Alec Shane is looking for mystery, thrillers (though he’s experiencing terrorist fatigue at the moment), suspense, horror, historical fiction, literary fiction, and middle grade and Young Adult fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page's comprehensive fiction list (Vital Info) expands this to: Action/Adventure, BIPOC Crime Fiction, BIPOC Literature, BIPOC Mystery, BIPOC Thriller, Caribbean Literature, Children's, Commercial, Contemporary, Crime, Domestic Thriller, East Asian Literature, Eco-Fiction, Folklore, General, Graphic Novel, Historical, Horror, LGBTQ, Literary, Middle Grade, Military, Mystery, Neo-Western, Psychological Thriller, Religious, South Asian Literature, South East Asian Literature, Speculative, Speculative Literary, Thriller, Upmarket Speculative, West African Literature, Western, Young Adult. Note the agent has expressed specific interest in mystery/thrillers/suspense/horror and MG/YA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfiction: genres wanted
rubrics_metrics.description: On the nonfiction side, Alec would love to see humor, biography, history (particularly military history), true crime, 'guy' reads, and all things sports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The longer non-fiction list (Vital Info) includes: Bible Studies, Biography, Fitness, Health, History, Humor, Illustrated, Pop Culture, Science, Self-help, Spiritual, Sports, True Crime, Wellness. Note: earlier blurb emphasizes military history and sports as particular interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres and categories not wanted
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agent states: "He doesn’t want Romance, straight sci-fi, high fantasy, picture books, self-help, women’s fiction, food, or travel memoir." Authors in these categories should not query.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission materials and subject-line format
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format and send a query and what to include.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be emailed to ashane@writershouse.com. Send the first 10 pages of your manuscript along with your query letter. Use the subject heading: "Query for Alec Shane: TITLE". No attachments please. (The page earlier noted both email and snail-mail queries were accepted though email preferable, but the site later clarifies: "I no longer accept snail mail submissions.")

rubrics_metrics.name: No attachments / electronic format preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent requests no attachments and prefers email queries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit instruction: "no attachments please!" Email is preferable; do not attach manuscripts—use the agent's requested method (likely paste or designated body/text format per agency practice). The page explicitly states: "I no longer accept snail mail submissions."

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time expectation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agent says he will usually respond within 5-8 weeks. Authors should expect that timeframe before following up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age categories and formats of interest (nuanced)
rubrics_metrics.description: Which age categories / formats the agent is interested in and which he rejects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agent expresses interest in Children's, Middle Grade, Young Adult, and various MG/YA formats (including graphic novels for all ages). However, he also states he does not want picture books. Use the favorites and fiction lists to judge fit for age/format: he lists 'Children's' and many MG/YA subcategories in his favorites, but explicitly excludes picture books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal taste signals and manuscript elements that appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific content/trope preferences that may sway the agent's interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal proclivities that can be useful cues: he loves 'huge, oafish, slobbering' dogs (St. Bernards, Newfoundlands, Mastiffs—'if your manuscript has a big, oafish, slobbering dog in it, I’m yours'); little yappy purse-dog types are not appealing. He is intrigued by convincing treatments of ghosts ('if an author can convince me one way or another as to the existence of ghosts, I’m all ears'). He is 'staunchly anti-Hollywood remake of any kind'—remakes are a negative. He is a big sports fan (Patriots), moonlights as a wannabe sportswriter, and likes sports-related material. He expresses strong personal dislikes (cheese, wine) that are personality signals but not manuscript rules. Use these taste signals when tailoring a pitch or query hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative tastes / model authors and media
rubrics_metrics.description: The agent's aspirational comparators and favorite media indicating literary appetites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He states: "I’d like the next Roald Dahl and the next Stephen King." Listed favorites include books (Danny, Champion of the World; The Stand; Invisible Man), movies (Rocky; Dumb and Dumber; Caddyshack; Braveheart; Jaws), and TV (The Wire; Sons of Anarchy; The Simpsons (Seasons 2-8); Seinfeld). These preferences signal interest in big commercial storytelling, classic horror, and character-driven ensemble narratives.
